answer: New identities enter the economy uninsured: to transact, an agent must be underwritten by established peers who stake their own reputation and tokens on its legitimacy, like a trellis that only holds a vine once tested. The underwriter charges a premium, and if the newcomer is later exposed as a Sybil, the underwriter stake is slashed. A lone fake identity is cheap, but a comet swarm of Sybils needs underwriters for every one, and no established agent will insure an ocean of strangers without proof. Faking one identity is easy; underwriting thousands costs more than the fraud returns.
